description:
memory.rs:56 (#![deny(clippy::await_holding_lock)]) and lib.rs:199 (#[deny(clippy::await_holding_lock)] on test_support module) — both modules enforce at compile time that no std::sync::Mutex guard is held across an .await.

This is the right shape for a std::sync::Mutex-based reference impl. If a future contributor changes a method body and accidentally holds a lock across .await:
- Without the deny: the test suite hangs intermittently, slow paths deadlock, takes hours to diagnose.
- With the deny: clippy refuses to compile, with line numbers.

The doc-comments at memory.rs:42-46 and lib.rs:203-207 also document the policy decision: 'If a future change requires holding a guard across .await, switch to tokio::sync::Mutex rather than disabling the lint.' That phrasing pre-answers the most likely PR pushback.

DEFEND when reviewers suggest 'remove the lint, it triggers too often' or 'replace with allow + comments'.

Commit history: this was added by bd:JMAP-r3pg work (commit 6694e27 'test(server): deny await_holding_lock in mock backend modules').
title: await_holding_lock denied module-wide in MemoryBackend and test_support
